ai.description: This 40–50 mm frog has a brown to greyish dorsum with scattered warts. It is distinguished by a dark triangular mark between the eyes and a prominent, pale-edged tympanum.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Limnonectes doriae* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-colored mask extending from the snout through the eye to the tympanum.
ai.habitat: *Limnonectes doriae* inhabits moist, shaded forest floors and stream banks within tropical evergreen forests, typically at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Burmese Wart Frog is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights actively foraging for small invertebrates along the muddy banks of forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Limnonectes doriae* reproduces via aquatic eggs laid in small forest streams. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, though specific clutch sizes remain undocumented.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Limnonectes doriae* occurs in Northeast India, specifically in states like Meghalaya and Mizoram, typically inhabiting low-to-mid elevation forests and stream margins.
ai.callDescription: The Burmese Wart Frog emits a series of short, high-pitched "tink" or "click" notes, typically heard near small, rocky forest streams.
